done:
The Lap Analysis screen now has a summary row, a pace trend chart and a lap table with incident badges.
- Summary row: fastest lap, median lap with its delta, consistency (std dev of the timed laps) and an Incidents tile. The tile has loading, error, "no events in this file" and "None" states.
- Trend chart, "Pace against the fastest lap": one bar per lap, drawn as delta to the fastest lap so the bars start at zero. The fastest lap is a flat tertiary cap with a bolt glyph. A dashed line marks the median delta.
- Untimed laps (out lap, no time, incomplete) keep their slot as a hollow circle, with the reason in the tooltip. The chart animates in on first build and respects disableAnimations.
- Clicking a bar or a table row selects that lap through selectedLapIndexProvider, so the Trace and Track map follow. The selected lap is outlined in the chart and highlighted in the table. There is an "Open in Trace" button. Hovering a bar lights its table row, and hovering a row lights its bar.
- Incidents are read session-wide once by sessionIncidentsProvider (features/lap_analysis/application) and cut into laps in Dart. They show as labelled badges in a new Incidents table column and as glyphs under the chart columns, with tooltips. Impacts give a count and seconds into the lap. Wheel-detached marks say FL/FR/RL/RR, and whether the wheel was already off when the lap began. A yellow flag is quoted as its code, not decoded. The chart and table draw immediately and the marks arrive when the events finish reading.
- PerLapBarChart gained optional highlight, marks, selectedIndex, hoveredIndex, onBarTap, onBarHover and animateIn. Existing callers are unchanged, and the fuel/energy tests and golden still pass.

data_findings:
All numbers below were queried from the samples.
- Incident events, all three samples. LastImpactMagnitude is a BOOLEAN with rows false -> true at 213.8 s -> false at 508.1 s in the Race only. Practice and Qualify have one `false` row. Yellow Flag State (UTINYINT) and WheelsDetached (value1..4, UTINYINT) are a single all-zero row in every sample.
- Across 37.6 min recorded (5.5 + 9.8 + 22.3), exactly two incidents exist, both Race impacts. No yellow flag or detached wheel has ever been recorded.
- No event table in any sample repeats a value in consecutive rows, so the file stores changes only. The impact count is a lower bound and a row is an impact; the boolean's polarity carries no meaning.
- The `true` state spans 294.3 s (213.8 -> 508.1 s, laps 2-6), so counting the state would blame laps 3-5 for a lap-2 impact.
- Ground Speed at 100 Hz steps +3.51 km/h within 0.06 s at 213.8 s and +7.91 at 508.1 s. The largest 0.06 s step anywhere else in the 22 min is +2.05. That supports reading the two rows as real contacts.
- The data holds no magnitude, so a kerb tap cannot be told from a crash.
- Sector1/2/3 Flag: codes 1, 3 and 11 observed, with 7-21 rows per table in Race/Practice and one row (11) in Qualify. 11 is the initial state. Meaning is unresolved (§15.4) and they were not used.
- Race pace (16 timed laps): 63.941-64.701 s, spread 0.760 s, median 64.208 s (+0.267 s), std dev 0.235 s. The fastest lap is lap 11 (display number).
- Corner-order re-check in SurfaceTypes: rows where one wheel differs, value1/3 vs value2/4, versus mean lateral G (`G Force Long`, positive = left). The value1/3 group sits 0.58, 0.50 and 1.22 G further left (Practice, Qualify, Race; n = 387/287, 850/982, 1571/1852). The sign agrees on all three samples and the size varies with the circuit, so only the sign supports FL/FR/RL/RR. The previous agent's +0.80/+0.46/+0.22 did not reproduce and was replaced.
spec_notes:
§8.3 Built in v0.11 (additions):

The lap table now opens with a trend chart and is annotated with what went wrong on each lap.

The chart plots each lap's delta to the fastest lap, not its time. The Race's 16 timed laps run 63.941-64.701 s. Bars of absolute time from zero would put every lap within 1.2 % of one height, and a truncated axis would lie about ratios. A delta starts at zero honestly and is §8.3's "delta to personal best". The fastest lap therefore has no height and is marked in the tertiary (the lap table's "fastest" colour) by a 4 px cap and a bolt glyph. A dashed line marks the median lap (+0.267 s in the Race), and the Consistency tile states the standard deviation (±0.235 s over 16 laps). A lap the game did not time (out lap, no time, incomplete) keeps its slot as a hollow circle whose tooltip gives the reason. A zero-height bar would say "as fast as the fastest" and a grey stub would say "a little slower", and neither is true. Clicking a bar or a row loads that lap into the Trace and Track map through selectedLapIndexProvider. Hover is mirrored both ways between chart column and table row.

Incidents (impacts, Yellow Flag State, WheelsDetached) are read session-wide once by sessionIncidentsProvider and cut into laps in Dart, so the derivation is pure and unit-tested. They appear as labelled badges in the table and as glyphs under the chart columns, both built from one `incidentMarks` so the two cannot disagree. Wheel corners use a local FL/FR/RL/RR mapping, to be replaced by the shared corner model. A yellow flag is quoted by its code and never interpreted. The table and chart draw at once and the marks arrive when the events finish reading.

PerLapBarChart gained optional params (highlight colour, per-lap marks lane, selected/hovered index, tap/hover callbacks, animateIn). fuel/energy is unchanged.

§14 roadmap, findings from building it:
1. LastImpactMagnitude is a BOOLEAN with no magnitude, and a row is an impact, not its value. In the Race it reads false, true at 213.8 s, false at 508.1 s. Counting the `true` state would blame laps 3-5 (294.3 s of state) for a lap-2 impact. Ground Speed steps +3.51 km/h at 213.8 s and +7.91 km/h at 508.1 s within 0.06 s, against +2.05 as the largest step elsewhere in 22 min, which supports reading both rows as real contacts. Counts are a lower bound, since no event table in any sample repeats a value in consecutive rows. A kerb tap cannot be told from a crash.
2. Across 37.6 min of recordings, the only incidents ever written are those two impacts. Yellow Flag State and WheelsDetached are a single all-zero row in every sample, so their derivations are exercised only on constructed series. Real data from a session with a yellow flag or a lost wheel is needed before either can be called verified.
3. Sector1/2/3 Flag holds codes 1, 3 and 11 (11 is the initial state) with 1-21 rows per table. The codes change on every lap in every sample, so they are not annotated. Decoding them is §15.4.
4. Corner order on an event table, re-checked: in SurfaceTypes, rows whose odd wheel is value1/3 show 0.58, 0.50 and 1.22 G more left lateral load than rows whose odd wheel is value2/4 (Practice, Qualify, Race). The sign is identical on all three samples, which supports FL/FR/RL/RR. The size varies with the circuit.
5. Future: if a session ever has enough laps for the trend to matter as a stint picture (an endurance recording), the delta chart's "every-nth label" thinning is already in place but has been exercised only to 20 columns.
